title: All About a Bright Bug
checkpoint: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about butterflies (the words "butterfly" and "caterpillar" are not yet decodable at this stage).
note_for_grown_ups: Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about butterflies (the words "butterfly" and "caterpillar" are not yet decodable at this stage).

pages.text: Ned spots a bright bug in the garden.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling noticing a bright orange and black butterfly resting on a cabbage leaf in the vegetable patch.

pages.text: A bug like this has a pair of big wings.
pages.illustration: A close-up of the butterfly, its two large patterned wings spread wide.

pages.text: A bug like this can be very bright.
pages.illustration: Several butterflies of different bright colours fluttering among the vegetable plants.

pages.text: A bug like this drinks from a flower.
pages.illustration: The butterfly perched on a flower, its long thin tube reaching into the petals.

pages.text: A bug like this lands bit by bit, then rests.
pages.illustration: The butterfly fluttering down and landing gently on a leaf, wings settling flat.

pages.text: A bug like this can fly from plant to plant.
pages.illustration: A split scene: a green caterpillar on one side, the same butterfly on the other.

pages.text: A bug like this rests in the sun to get warm.
pages.illustration: A soft green chrysalis hanging from a stem, cracking open as a butterfly starts to emerge.

pages.text: Ned looks hard at the bright wings.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling leaning in close, examining the patterned wings of the butterfly.

pages.text: The bug lifts off the leaf.
pages.illustration: The butterfly taking off from the cabbage leaf, wings beating upward.

pages.text: Bugs like this are fun to spot in the garden.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling watching the butterfly flutter away over the rows of vegetables.
